# PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS] Contents of this Part

## I SCOPE OF THIS PART AND INTERPRETATION

## Part 6 rules about service apply generally

## 6.1 This Part applies to the service of documents, except where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.1 This Part applies to the service of documents, except where –] (a) another Part, any other enactment or a practice direction makes different provision; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.1 This Part applies to the service of documents, except where –] (b) the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.1 This Part applies to the service of documents, except where –] (Other Parts, for example, Part 54 (Judicial Review) and Part 55 (Possession Claims) contain specific provisions about service.)

## Interpretation

## 6.2 In this Part –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.2 In this Part –] (a) ‘bank holiday’ means a bank holiday under the Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971 1 in the part of the United Kingdom where service is to take place;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.2 In this Part –] (b) ‘business day’ means any day except Saturday, Sunday, a bank holiday, Good Friday or Christmas Day;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.2 In this Part –] (c) ‘claim’ includes petition and any application made before action or to commence proceedings and ‘claim form’, ‘claimant’ and ‘defendant’ are to be construed accordingly;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.2 In this Part –] (d) ‘solicitor’ includes any other person who, for the purposes of the Legal Services Act 2007, is an authorised person in relation to an activity which constitutes the conduct of litigation (within the meaning of that Act)

## II SERVICE OF THE CLAIM FORM IN THE JURISDICTION

## Methods of service

## 6.3

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (1) A claim form may  be served by any of the following methods –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (a) personal service in accordance with rule 6.5;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (b) first class post, document exchange or other service which provides for delivery on the next business day, in accordance with Practice Direction 6A;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (c) leaving it at a place specified in rule 6.7, 6.8, 6.9 or 6.10;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (d) fax or other means of electronic communication in accordance with Practice Direction 6A; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (e) any method authorised by the court under rule 6.15. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (2) A company may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (a) by any method permitted under this Part; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (b) by any of the methods of service permitted under the Companies Act 2006 2 . [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (3) A limited liability partnership may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (a) by any method permitted under this Part; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.3] (b) by any of the methods of service permitted under the Companies Act 2006 3 as applied with modification by regulations made under the Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2000 4 . ## Who is to serve the claim form

## 6.4

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (1) The court will serve the claim form except where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (a) a rule or practice direction provides that the claimant must serve it;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (b) the claimant notifies the court that the claimant wishes to serve it; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (c) the court orders or directs otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (2) Where the court is to serve the claim form, it is for the court to decide which method of service is to be used. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (3) Where the court is to serve the claim form, the claimant must, in addition to filing a copy for the court, provide a copy for each defendant to be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (4) Where the court has sent –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (a) a notification of outcome of postal service to the claimant in accordance with rule 6.18; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.4] (b) a notification of non-service by a bailiff in accordance with rule 6.19, the court will not try to serve the claim form again. ## Personal service

## 6.5

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (1) Where required by another Part, any other enactment, a practice direction or a court order, a claim form must be served personally. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (2) In other cases, a claim form may be served personally except –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (a) where rule 6.7 applies; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (b) in any proceedings against the Crown. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (Part 54 contains provisions about judicial review claims and Part 66 contains provisions about Crown proceedings.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (3) A claim form is served personally on –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (a) an individual by leaving it with that individual;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (b) a company or other corporation by leaving it with a person holding a senior position within the company or corporation; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (c) a partnership (where partners are being sued in the name of their firm) by leaving it with –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (i) a partner; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (ii) a person who, at the time of service, has the control or management of the partnership business at its principal place of business. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.5] (Practice Direction 6A sets out the meaning of ‘senior position’.)

## Where to serve the claim form – general provisions

## 6.6

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.6] (1) The claim form must be served within the jurisdiction except where rule 6.7(2) or 6.11 applies or as provided by Section IV of this Part. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.6] (2) The claimant must include in the claim form an address at which the defendant may be served. That address must include a full postcode, unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.6] (3) Paragraph (2) does not apply where an order made by the court under rule 6.15 (service by an alternative method or at an alternative place) specifies the place or method of service of the claim form. ## Service on a solicitor or within the United Kingdom

## 6.7

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (1) Solicitor within the jurisdiction: Subject to rule 6.5(1), where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (a) the defendant has given in writing the business address within the jurisdiction of a solicitor as an address at which the defendant may be served with the claim form; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (b) a solicitor acting for the defendant has notified the claimant in writing that the solicitor is instructed by the defendant to accept service of the claim form on behalf of the defendant at a business address within the jurisdiction,

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] the claim form must be served at the business address of that solicitor. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (‘Solicitor’ has the extended meaning set out in rule 6.2(d).)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (2) Solicitor in Scotland or Northern Ireland: Subject to rule 6.5(1) and the provisions of Section IV of this Part, and except where any other rule or practice direction makes different provision, where—

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (a) the defendant has given in writing the business address in Scotland or Northern Ireland of a solicitor as an address at which the defendant may be served with the claim form;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (aa) a solicitor acting for the defendant has notified the claimant in writing that the solicitor is instructed by the defendant to accept service of the claim form on behalf of the defendant at a business address within Scotland or Northern Ireland;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (b) [Omitted]

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (c) [Omitted]

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] the claim form must be served at the business address of that solicitor. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] 6.8 Subject to rules 6.5(1) and 6.7  except where any other rule or practice direction makes different provision –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (a) the defendant may be served with the claim form at an address at which the defendant resides or carries on business within the UK  and which the defendant has given for the purpose of being served with the proceedings; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (b) in any claim by a tenant or contract-holder against a landlord, the claim form may be served at an address given by the landlord under section 48 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1987 or section 39 of the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (For Production Centre Claims see paragraph 2.3(7A) of Practice Direction 7B; for Money Claims Online see paragraph 4(6) of Practice Direction 7C; and for Possession Claims Online see paragraph 5.1(4) of Practice Direction 55B.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.7] (For service out of the jurisdiction see rules 6.40 to 6.47.)

## 6.9

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (1) This rule applies where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (a) rule 6.5(1) (personal service);

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (b) rule 6.7 (service of claim form on solicitor); and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (c) rule 6.8 (defendant gives address at which the defendant may be served), do not apply and the claimant does not wish to effect personal service under rule 6.5(2). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (2) Subject to paragraphs (3) to (6), the claim form must be served on the defendant at the place shown in the following table. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (For service out of the jurisdiction see rules 6.40 to 6.47.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (3) Where a claimant has reason to believe that the address of the defendant referred to in entries 1, 2 or 3 in the table in paragraph (2) is an address at which the defendant no longer resides or carries on business, the claimant must take reasonable steps to ascertain the address of the defendant’s current residence or place of business (‘current address’). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (4) Where, having taken the reasonable steps required by paragraph (3), the claimant –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (a) ascertains the defendant’s current address, the claim form must be served at that address; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (b) is unable to ascertain the defendant’s current address, the claimant must consider whether there is –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (i) an alternative place where; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (ii) an alternative method by which,

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] service may be effected. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (5) If, under paragraph (4)(b), there is such a place where or a method by which service may be effected, the claimant must make an application under rule 6.15. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (6) Where paragraph (3) applies, the claimant may serve on the defendant’s usual or last known address in accordance with the table in paragraph (2) where the claimant –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (a) cannot ascertain the defendant’s current residence or place of business; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.9] (b) cannot ascertain an alternative place or an alternative method under paragraph (4)(b). ## Service of the claim form in proceedings against the Crown

## 6.10 In proceedings against the Crown –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.10 In proceedings against the Crown –] (a) service on the Attorney General must be effected on the Treasury Solicitor; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.10 In proceedings against the Crown –] (b) service on a government department must be effected on the solicitor acting for that department. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.10 In proceedings against the Crown –] (Practice Direction 66 gives the list published under section 17 of the Crown Proceedings Act 1947 6 of the solicitors acting in civil proceedings (as defined in that Act) for the different government departments on whom service is to be effected, and of their addresses.)

## Service of the claim form by contractually agreed method

## 6.11

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.11] (1) Where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.11] (a) a contract contains a term providing that, in the event of a claim being started in relation to the contract, the claim form may be served by a method or at a place specified in the contract; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.11] (b) a claim solely in respect of that contract is started, the claim form may, subject to paragraph (2), be served on the defendant by the method or at the place specified in the contract. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.11] (2) Where in accordance with the contract the claim form is to be served out of the jurisdiction, it may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.11] (a) if permission to serve it out of the jurisdiction has been granted under rule 6.36; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.11] (b) without permission under rule 6.32 or 6.33. ## 6.12

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (1) The court may, on application, permit a claim form relating to a contract to be served on the defendant’s agent where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (a) the defendant is out of the jurisdiction;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (b) the contract to which the claim relates was entered into within the jurisdiction with or through the defendant’s agent; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (c) at the time of the application either the agent’s authority has not been terminated or the agent is still in business relations with the defendant. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (2) An application under this rule –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (a) must be supported by evidence setting out –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (i) details of the contract and that it was entered into within the jurisdiction or through an agent who is within the jurisdiction;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (ii) that the principal for whom the agent is acting was, at the time the contract was entered into and is at the time of the application, out of the jurisdiction; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (iii) why service out of the jurisdiction cannot be effected; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (b) may be made without notice. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (3) An order under this rule must state the period within which the defendant must respond to the particulars of claim. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (4) Where the court makes an order under this rule –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (a) a copy of the application notice and the order must be served with the claim form on the agent; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (b) unless the court orders otherwise, the claimant must send to the defendant a copy of the application notice, the order and the claim form. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.12] (5) This rule does not exclude the court’s power under rule 6.15 (service by an alternative method or at an alternative place). ## Service of the claim form on children and protected parties

## 6.13

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (1) Where the defendant is a child who is not also a protected party, the claim form must be served on –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (a) one of the child’s parents or guardians; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (b) if there is no parent or guardian, an adult with whom the child resides or in whose care the child is. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (2) Where the defendant is a protected party, the claim form must be served on –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (a) one of the following persons with authority in relation to the protected party as –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (i) the attorney under a registered enduring power of attorney;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (ii) the donee of a lasting power of attorney; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (iii) the deputy appointed by the Court of Protection; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (b) if there is no such person, an adult with whom the protected party resides or in whose care the protected party is. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (3) Any reference in this Section to a defendant or a party to be served includes the person to be served with the claim form on behalf of a child or protected party under paragraph (1) or (2). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (4) The court may make an order permitting a claim form to be served on a child or protected party, or on a person other than the person specified in paragraph (1) or (2). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (5) An application for an order under paragraph (4) may be made without notice. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (6) The court may order that, although a claim form has been sent or given to someone other than the person specified in paragraph (1) or (2), it is to be treated as if it had been properly served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (7) This rule does not apply where the court has made an order under rule 21.2(3) allowing a child to conduct proceedings without a litigation friend. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.13] (Part 21 contains rules about the appointment of a litigation friend and ‘child’ and ‘protected party’ have the same meaning as in rule 21.1.)

## Deemed service

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed service] 6.14 A claim form served within the United Kingdom in accordance with this Part is deemed to be served on the second business day after completion of the relevant step under rule 7.5(1). ## Service of the claim form by an alternative method or at an alternative place

## 6.15

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (1) Where it appears to the court that there is a good reason to authorise service by a method or at a place not otherwise permitted by this Part, the court may make an order permitting service by an alternative method or at an alternative place. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (2) On an application under this rule, the court may order that steps already taken to bring the claim form to the attention of the defendant by an alternative method or at an alternative place is good service. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (3) An application for an order under this rule –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (a) must be supported by evidence; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (b) may be made without notice. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (4) An order under this rule must specify –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (a) the method or place of service;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (b) the date on which the claim form is deemed served; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (c) the period for –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (i) filing an acknowledgment of service;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (ii) filing an admission; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.15] (iii) filing a defence. ## Power of court to dispense with service of the claim form

## 6.16

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.16] (1) The court may dispense with service of a claim form in exceptional circumstances. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.16] (2) An application for an order to dispense with service may be made at any time and –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.16] (a) must be supported by evidence; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.16] (b) may be made without notice. ## Notice and certificate of service relating to the claim form

## 6.17

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.17] (1) Where the court serves a claim form, the court will send to the claimant a notice which will include the date on which the claim form is deemed served under rule 6.14. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.17] (2) Where the claimant serves the claim form, the claimant –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.17] (a) must file a certificate of service within 21 days of service of the particulars of claim, unless all the defendants to the proceedings have filed acknowledgments of service within that time; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.17] (b) may not obtain judgment in default under Part 12 unless a certificate of service has been filed. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.17] (3) The certificate of service must state –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.17] (a) where rule 6.7, 6.8, 6.9 or 6.10 applies, the category of address at which the claimant believes the claim form has been served; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.17] (b) the details set out in the following table. ## Notification of outcome of postal service by the court

## 6.18

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.18] (1) Where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.18] (a) the court serves the claim form by post; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.18] (b) the claim form is returned to the court,

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.18] the court will send notification to the claimant that the claim form has been returned. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.18] (2) The claim form will be deemed to be served unless the address for the defendant on the claim form is not the relevant address for the purpose of rules 6.7 to 6.10. ## Notice of non-service by bailiff

## 6.19 Where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.19 Where –] (a) the court bailiff is to serve a claim form; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.19 Where –] (b) the bailiff is unable to serve it on the defendant,

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.19 Where –] the court will send notification to the claimant. ## III SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS OTHER THAN THE CLAIM FORM IN THE UNITED KINGDOM

## Methods of service

## 6.20

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (1) A document may be served by any of the following methods –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (a) personal service, in accordance with rule 6.22;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (b) first class post, document exchange or other service which provides for delivery on the next business day, in accordance with Practice Direction 6A;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (c) leaving it at a place specified in rule 6.23;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (d) fax or other means of electronic communication in accordance with Practice Direction 6A; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (e) any method authorised by the court under rule 6.27. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (2) A company may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (a) by any method permitted under this Part; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (b) by any of the methods of service permitted under the Companies Act 2006. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (3) A limited liability partnership may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (a) by any method permitted under this Part; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (b) by any of the methods of service permitted under the Companies Act 2006 as applied with modification by regulations made under the Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2000. ## Who is to serve

## 6.21

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (1) A party to proceedings will serve a document which that party has prepared except where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (a) a rule or practice direction provides that the court will serve the document; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (b) the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (2) The court will serve a document which it has prepared except where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (a) a rule or practice direction provides that a party must serve the document;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (b) the party on whose behalf the document is to be served notifies the court that the party wishes to serve it; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (c) the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (3) Where the court is to serve a document, it is for the court to decide which method of service is to be used. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (4) Where the court is to serve a document prepared by a party, that party must provide a copy for the court and for each party to be served. ## Personal service

## 6.22

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (1) Where required by another Part, any other enactment, a practice direction or a court order, a document must be served personally. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (2) In other cases, a document may be served personally except –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (a) where the party to be served has given an address for service under rule 6.23; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (b) in any proceedings by or against the Crown. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (3) A document may be served personally as if the document were a claim form in accordance with rule 6.5(3). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (For service out of the jurisdiction see rules 6.40 to 6.47.)

## Address for service to be given after proceedings are started

## 6.23

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (1) Unless the court orders otherwise, a party to proceedings must give an address at which that party may be served with documents relating to those proceedings. The address must include a full postcode. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (2) Except where any other rule, practice direction or order makes different provision, a party’s address for service must be –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (a) the business address within the United Kingdom of a solicitor acting for the party to be served; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (b) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (c) where there is no solicitor acting for the party –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (i) an address within the United Kingdom at which the party resides or carries on business;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (For Production Centre Claims see paragraph 2.3(7) and (7A) of Practice Direction 7B; for Money Claims Online see paragraph 4(3A) and (6) of Practice Direction 7C; and for Possession Claims Online see paragraph 5.1(3A) and (4) of Practice Direction 55B.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (3) Where none of sub-paragraphs (2)(a) or (c) applies unless the court orders otherwise, the party must give an address for service within the United Kingdom. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (Part 42 contains provisions about change of solicitor. Rule 42.1 provides that where a party gives the business address of a solicitor as that party’s address for service, that solicitor will be considered to be acting for the party until the provisions of Part 42 are complied with.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (4) Subject to the provisions of Section IV of this Part (where applicable), any document to be served in proceedings must be sent or transmitted to, or left at, the party’s address for service under paragraph (2) or (3) unless it is to be served personally or the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (5) Where, in accordance with Practice Direction 6A, a party indicates or is deemed to have indicated that they will accept service by fax, the fax number given by that party must be at the address for service. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (6) Where a party indicates in accordance with Practice Direction 6A that they will accept service by electronic means other than fax, the e-mail address or electronic identification given by that party will be deemed to be at the address for service. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (7) In proceedings by or against the Crown, service of any document in the proceedings on the Crown must be effected in the same manner prescribed in rule 6.10 as if the document were a claim form. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (8) This rule does not apply where an order made by the court under rule 6.27 (service by an alternative method or at an alternative place) specifies where a document may be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (For service out of the jurisdiction see rules 6.40 to 6.47.)

## Change of address for service

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Change of address for service] 6.24 Where the address for service of a party changes, that party must give notice in writing of the change as soon as it has taken place to the court and every other party.
